the composition of modern sands in the Junggar, Turpan, and Tarim basins of western Xinjiang, China, reflects a complex history of tectonically induced changes in sediment sources.
the composition of modern sand of the basins of Xinjiaing Uygur Autonomous Re gion, northwest China, reflects the complicated tecton ic history of sediment-source areas.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of tectonic setting on the provenance and composition of modern sands of the Xinjiang basins of western central Asia, and the application of these data to understanding of the composition of ancient sands of collisional successor basin systems.
the influence of tectonic heritage on sandstone composition and the use of detrital petrology to infer tectonic setting.
the impact of tectonic history on sand composition and the implications for provenance interpretation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sand composition is an unreliable indicator of tectonic setting for basins of complex tectonic history.

sand composition in collisional successor basin settings is a poor indicator of the present tectonic setting, and that the composition is more strongly controlled by the composition of the accreted basement terranes.

the composition of modern Xinjiang basin sands reflects derivation from a complicated tectonic collage of terranes, and the composition of the sand does not necessarily reflect the tectonic setting in which the basin is currently located.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tectonic setting inferred from sandstone detrial modes is strongly influenced by the tectonic history and composition of the sediment source terrane.
sandstone composition of collisional successor-basin sands is controlled by tectonic setting in a general way, but also by the tectonic history (and hence, composition) of source terranes.
sand composition is a useful provenance indicator in collisional successor basains only if the tectonic setting is known and the composition of potential source terranes is well constrained.
The main takeaway from our work is that
provenance studies must be interpreted with caution when applied to basins of complex tectonic history.

the tectonic setting for sandstone detritus is not necessarily the same as that of the basin in which it is deposited, and that the tectonics of sediment source terranes must be considered in interpreting sandstone composition.
the composition of sand in a sedimentary basin does not necessarily reflect the tectonic setting or tectonic history at the time of deposition.
